title: Interleaved Burst Protection and Reservation Drivers PRD
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: Customers running latency-sensitive workloads on Redwood Dedicated pools see unpredictable tail latency and failures during cross-tenant burst events. Existing reserved pools + autoscaler do not coordinate with emergency burst handling, resulting in either overreaction (overprovisioning) or underprovisioning (preemptive eviction of business-critical tenants).

This PRD defines a coordinated feature set ("Interleaved Burst Protection and Reservation Drivers") to harmonize reserved pool accounting, autoscaler signals, and burst fallback policies so Dedicated tenants get predictable degradation envelopes and operators can reason about capacity shifts during surges.
goals: Provide a deterministic fallback behavior for tenants when cluster-wide burst events occur
Unify reserved pool accounting with autoscaler signals so headroom is visible and actionable
Enable per-tenant degradation profiles (soft-qos) that preserve critical requests while shedding non-critical load
Expose metrics and alerts for burst contention, borrow events, and preemption actions
Ship a minimal operator UI surface in Console for tuning reservation drivers and emergency borrow policies
non_goals: Replace long-term capacity planning or billing model changes
Support custom kernel/runtime level optimizations (this is an orchestration-layer feature)
Implement tenant-level application rewriting to reduce token counts
solution_overview: Introduce a reservation driver service that sits in the Dedicated control plane and mediates between Reserve allocations, autoscaler suggestions, and the runtime fallback engine. It will: 1) maintain a 'headroom ledger' per zone/pool calculated from live metrics and reserved commitments; 2) publish normalized autoscale intent signals (scale_up_intent, scale_down_intent, emergency_borrow_intent) to the runtime; 3) enact bounded emergency borrow windows with tenant-credit accounting; 4) expose tenant degradation profiles (preserve priority routes and route-level timeouts).
functional_requirements: Driver must compute headroom every 30s using live GPU utilization, queued requests, and reserved slot counts
Driver must expose three intents: scale_up_intent, scale_down_intent, emergency_borrow_intent via control-plane API
Emergency borrow can reassign up to X% (configurable, default 10%) of idle reserved capacity for non-critical bursts for up to N minutes (configurable, default 5 minutes)
Support tenant credit ledger: track borrowed seconds and credits; a tenant that borrows must be charged or penalized per policy
Provide per-tenant degradation profile that maps request classes to actions: allow, queue-with-timeout, reject-with-fallback
Console feature flag and tuning panel for reservation driver parameters per pool
Telemetry: emitted events for borrow-grant, borrow-revoke, preemption-start, preemption-complete with tenant_id, pool_id, reason
nonfunctional_requirements: Decision latency: driver intent updates must be available within 500ms of metrics window completion
Consistency: headroom ledger must converge within 3s across control-plane replicas
Resilience: driver must tolerate a transient loss of metrics (up to 60s) and revert to conservative defaults
Safety: emergency borrow defaults must never exceed configured percent thresholds and must respect tenant isolation contracts
Observability: all actions should be logged and queryable in Console within 2 minutes
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end test: simulated cross-tenant burst causes a borrow event and borrower receives at most configured % of idle capacity and borrow window honors configured duration
SLO: under a defined synthetic burst load, top-10% latency for reserved tenant priority routes increases no more than factor 2 within first 10 minutes and critical route success rate remains >= 99%
Metric availability: headroom and borrow events surface in Console dashboards and can be queried via API within retention window
Operator controls: Console panel allows toggling emergency borrow and adjusting max-borrow-percent and borrow-window; changes apply within 60s
No regressions: existing autoscaler scale-up and scale-down behaviors remain functional when driver is disabled (feature flag off)
rollout_plan: 1) Feature gated dev rollout in staging with synthetic tenant-burst test harness (2 weeks). 2) Canary enablement on a subset of Dedicated clusters with low-impact tenants (1 week). 3) Gradual ramp to 25% of traffic while monitoring key metrics (2 weeks). 4) Full tenant opt-in and operator training + docs (1 week).
telemetry_and_alerting: alert: sustained headroom < configured-min for > 5 minutes (capacity team)
security_and_compliance: No new tenant data will be exfiltrated. Driver uses existing control-plane auth. Audit logs for borrow/grant actions must be retained and forwarded to customer's audit stream when running in Private/VPC mode.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: aggressive borrow could violate isolation guarantees -> Mitigation: hard caps, conservative defaults, and automatic rollback on complaints
Risk: control-plane race conditions cause oscillation between scale intents -> Mitigation: add dampening window and hysteresis in decision logic
Risk: inaccurate headroom due to noisy metrics -> Mitigation: median-of-windows and fallback to conservative estimate
open_questions: Should borrow be billable as premium usage or consume pre-paid reservations? (billing impact)
What are tenant-level priority signals (route tags, SLA labels) we should honor by default?
Do we allow cross-zone borrow or restrict to same availability zone?
dependencies_notes: Depends on ENG-22890 (autoscaler signal normalization) and a lightweight runtime hook to accept emergency_borrow_intent (ENG-23011). Console UI work depends on Console-UI sprint cycle 2026.04.
implementation_timeline: Week 1-2: design finalization, API spec and driver prototype
Week 3-4: driver implementation, control-plane integration, autoscale normalization
Week 5: runtime hook and small runtime change to accept intents
Week 7-8: staging tests, canary rollout, docs
notes: This PRD intentionally focuses on orchestration-level controls rather than runtime kernel changes.
We expect several follow-ups: billing model for borrow, finer-grained tenant credit reconciliation, and per-route quality-of-service policies.
